dervis-irab:1-7.t:
* Vocabulary:
(الرُّومُ): what history says about them will come in the section on benefits.
(بِضْعِ سِنِينَ): the meaning of biḍʿ and the scholars' disagreement about its number preceded in Sūrat Yūsuf; al-Aṣmaʿī chose that it is from three to ten.

* I'rab:
(الم غُلِبَتِ الرُّومُ): the discussion of the i'rab of (الم) has preceded. (غلبت) is a passive past verb and (الروم) is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent).
(فِي أَدْنَى الْأَرْضِ وَهُمْ مِنْ بَعْدِ غَلَبِهِمْ سَيَغْلِبُونَ): (في أدنى) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) (غلبت); the wāw is a conjunction; (هم) is a mubtadaʾ (subject); the preposition and its genitive noun (من بعد غلبهم) are attached to His saying (سيغلبون); (غلبهم) is the maṣdar (verbal noun) of the passive verb, annexed to its object; and the clause (سيغلبون) is the predicate of the mubtadaʾ.
(فِي بِضْعِ سِنِينَ لِلَّهِ الْأَمْرُ مِنْ قَبْلُ وَمِنْ بَعْدُ): (في بضع سنين) is also attached to His saying (سيغلبون); the secret of leaving the number of years vague will come in the section on rhetoric. (لله) is a fronted predicate and (الأمر) a postponed subject. The clause is resumptive, as if it were the answer to an implied question, namely: what is the benefit of mentioning His saying (من بعد غلبهم), since His saying (سيغلبون) can only be after the defeat? The answer is that its benefit is to show the completeness of power and to make clear that this is by the command of Allah the Exalted alone. (من قبل) is attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial); (من) is a preposition, and (قبل) and (بعد) are two adverbs made indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma because they are cut off from annexation in wording [Translator's note: the source has the misprint «لقظا» for «لفظا»] but not in meaning; then they were made genitive by (من) and remained with their ḍamma, i.e. before the defeat of the Romans and after it.
(وَيَوْمَئِذٍ يَفْرَحُ الْمُؤْمِنُونَ بِنَصْرِ اللَّهِ يَنْصُرُ مَنْ يَشاءُ وَهُوَ الْعَزِيزُ الرَّحِيمُ): the wāw is a conjunction; (يومئذ) is an adverb annexed to its like, attached to (يفرح), and the tanwīn is a substitute for a clause, as has preceded, i.e. "on the day the Romans overcome"; (بنصر الله) is also attached to (يفرح). The clause (ينصر من يشاء) is resumptive, to show the truthfulness of the believers; (من) is a relative noun, the object of (ينصر), and the clause (يشاء) is the ṣila (relative clause); (هو) is a mubtadaʾ, (العزيز) a first predicate and (الرحيم) a second predicate.
(وَعْدَ اللَّهِ لا يُخْلِفُ اللَّهُ وَعْدَهُ وَلكِنَّ أَكْثَرَ النَّاسِ لا يَعْلَمُونَ): (وعد الله) is a maṣdar emphasizing the content of the preceding clause, namely His saying (سيغلبون) and (ويفرح المؤمنون). The clause (لا يخلف الله وعده) is either explicative, affirming the meaning of the maṣdar, and so has no grammatical position, or a ḥāl from the maṣdar. The wāw is circumstantial; lākinna and its noun, and the clause «لا يعملون» [Translator's note: so in the source, a misprint for «لا يعلمون»] is its predicate.
(يَعْلَمُونَ ظاهِراً مِنَ الْحَياةِ الدُّنْيا وَهُمْ عَنِ الْآخِرَةِ هُمْ غافِلُونَ): concerning the clause (يعلمون), it was said that it is resumptive, and this is a sound view to which there is no objection. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "It is a badal (substitute) from His saying «يعلمون» [Translator's note: so in the source; al-Zamakhsharī's text has «لا يعلمون»]. The subtle point in this substitution is that He substituted it for it and made it such that it takes its place and fills its position, to let you know that there is no difference between the absence of knowledge, which is ignorance, and the presence of a knowledge that does not go beyond this world. His saying (ظاهرا من الحياة الدنيا) conveys that this world has an outward and an inward aspect. Its outward aspect is what the ignorant know of enjoying its ornaments and taking pleasure in its delights; its inward aspect and reality is that it is a passage to the Hereafter, from which provision is taken for it through obedience and righteous deeds." Al-Zamakhsharī's view is more firmly rooted in eloquence and fuller of rhetoric, but substituting the affirmative for the negative is not sound, as the rules of grammar stipulate. (هم) is a mubtadaʾ; (عن الآخرة) is attached to (غافلون); the second (هم) is a tawkīd (emphasis) of the first (هم); and (غافلون) is the predicate of the first (هم). The second (هم) may also be a second mubtadaʾ whose predicate is (غافلون), the clause being the predicate of the first (هم).

* Rhetoric:
1- Vagueness (ibhām):
In His saying «في بضع سنين» there is vagueness. Its benefit is magnification, putting fear into the hearts of the polytheists at every moment, and intimating that their pride in themselves and their reliance on their strength last only for a time, long or short, but are bound to come to an end and lead to the inevitable outcome, which is reversal and relapse. Vagueness has been mentioned many times before.
2- Indefiniteness (tankīr):
That is in His saying «يعلمون ظاهرا من الحياة الدنيا». Its benefit is to make what they know small, and making it small brings it close to negation, so that it matches the one substituted for, namely His saying «لا يعلمون». This is what makes the substitution analysis preferable [Translator's note: the source has «البالية», apparently a misprint for «البدلية» (the substitution analysis)]. How excellent al-Zamakhsharī is! How deep his insight and how polished his mind! It is reported from al-Ḥasan that he said, when reciting this verse: "One of them reached such accuracy in the outward life of this world that he would tap the dinar with his finger and know whether it was good or bad." In this there is a diminishing [Translator's note: the source has «تعليل» (giving the reason), apparently a misprint for «تقليل» (diminishing)] of the knowledge which reached its furthest limits, plunged into the depths of the sea, soared into the expanses of space, and perceived the most remote secrets and hidden thoughts; but when it confronts the hidden secrets of the universe, such as the beginning, the return and the final end, it stands insignificant, able neither to begin nor to repeat.
3- Recurrence (taʿaṭṭuf):
In His saying «وهم عن الآخرة هم غافلون» there is the device of taʿaṭṭuf, which is the repetition of the very same word within a sentence of speech or a line of poetry. He repeated «هم» for hyperbole in emphasizing their heedlessness of the Hereafter.

* Benefits:
What history says:
(الرُّومُ): a name the Arabs applied to the Byzantines, and which today is applied to the Eastern Melkite Christians, Catholic and Orthodox. The Eastern Roman Empire was known as the Byzantine, after Byzantium, the old name of Constantinople; the Arabs called its inhabitants al-Rūm. The first of the Byzantine emperors — his father Theodosius divided the empire into a western one, with its capital Rome, and an eastern one, with its capital Constantinople [Translator's note: the sentence is incomplete in the source; the emperor's name is not given].
The occasion of the revelation of the verse is that there was fighting between Persia and the Romans. The Romans and Persia fought between Adhriʿāt and Buṣrā, and Persia defeated the Romans. The news reached Mecca, and it grieved the Prophet and the Muslims, because the Persians were Magians with no scripture, while the Romans were People of the Book. The polytheists rejoiced and gloated, and said to the Muslims: "You are People of the Book, and the Christians are People of the Book, while we are unlettered and the Persians are unlettered; our brothers among the people of Persia have prevailed over your brothers among the Romans, and we shall surely prevail over you." So it was revealed. Abū Bakr said to them: "May Allah not delight your eyes; by Allah, the Romans will surely prevail over Persia after a few years." Ubayy ibn Khalaf said to him: "You lie." Al-Ṣiddīq said to him: "You are the greater liar, O enemy of Allah." He said: "Set a term between us and I will wager with you on it" — al-munāḥaba, with the undotted ḥāʾ, is wagering. So he wagered with him on ten young she-camels from each of them, and they set the term at three years. Abū Bakr informed the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who said: "That is not what I mentioned; biḍʿ is only between three and nine. So increase the stake and extend the term." So they made it one hundred young she-camels for nine years. When Ubayy ibn Khalaf feared that Abū Bakr would leave, he came to him, held on to him and said: "I fear that you will leave Mecca, so appoint a guarantor for me." His son ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Bakr stood guarantor for him. When Ubayy wanted to go out to Uḥud, ʿAbd Allāh came to him, held on to him and said: "No, by Allah, I will not leave you until you give me a guarantor." So he gave him a guarantor, then went out to Uḥud, then returned to Mecca and died there of the wound which the Prophet had inflicted on him when he fought him in single combat. The Romans prevailed over Persia on the day of al-Ḥudaybiya, and that was at the end of seven years from their wager. Abū Bakr took the stake from Ubayy's heirs and brought it to the Messenger of Allah, who said to him: "Give it in charity." [Translator's note: the entry ends here in the source.]

dervis-irab:30-32.t:
* Vocabulary:
(حِزْبٍ): al-ḥizb is a group of people; weapons; a man's soldiers and companions who share his opinion; a share; a portion of the Qur'an or of something else. The plural is aḥzāb. Every people whose hearts and deeds resemble one another are aḥzāb, even if they have not met one another.

* I'rab:
(فَأَقِمْ وَجْهَكَ لِلدِّينِ حَنِيفاً) The fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the eloquent fāʾ, which discloses an omitted clause). أقم is an imperative verb, its agent a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "you". وجهك is a direct object (mafʿūl bihi). للدين is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) أقم. حنيفا is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent of أقم, or from its object, or from الدين. (فِطْرَتَ اللَّهِ الَّتِي فَطَرَ النَّاسَ عَلَيْها) It is a direct object of an omitted verb, i.e. "Cleave to the fiṭra of Allah", meaning His creation. We implied it in the address to a plural audience because of what comes later, منيبين إليه, as will follow. It was also said that it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) of an omitted verb, i.e. "He created you with a creation (faṭarakum fiṭratan)". التي is an adjective (naʿt) of الفطرة, the clause فطر الناس is the ṣila (relative clause), and عليها is attached to فطر. (لا تَبْدِيلَ لِخَلْقِ اللَّهِ) The sentence gives the reason for the command to cleave to His fiṭra. لا is the lā of generic negation, تبديل is its noun, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, and لخلق الله is the predicate. (ذلِكَ الدِّينُ الْقَيِّمُ وَلكِنَّ أَكْثَرَ النَّاسِ لا يَعْلَمُونَ) ذلك is the subject (mubtadaʾ), الدين its predicate (khabar), and القيم an adjective. The wāw is circumstantial or resumptive. ولكن is lākinna with its noun, and the clause لا يعلمون is its predicate. (مُنِيبِينَ إِلَيْهِ وَاتَّقُوهُ وَأَقِيمُوا الصَّلاةَ وَلا تَكُونُوا مِنَ الْمُشْرِكِينَ) منيبين is a ḥāl from the implied agent of الزموا, as we indicated above; this is better than making it a ḥāl from the agent of أقم. واتقوا الله is conjoined to the implied الزموا, and likewise the words وأقيموا الصلاة. لا is prohibitive, تكونوا is an imperfect defective verb (kāna), jussive by the prohibitive lā, and the wāw is its noun, and من المشركين is its predicate. (مِنَ الَّذِينَ فَرَّقُوا دِينَهُمْ وَكانُوا شِيَعاً) من الذين is a badal (substitute) for the words من المشركين, with repetition of the governing particle. The clause فرقوا دينهم is the ṣila. وكانوا شيعا: kāna, its noun and its predicate. (كُلُّ حِزْبٍ بِما لَدَيْهِمْ فَرِحُونَ) كل حزب is the subject; بما is attached to فرحون; the adverbial لديهم is attached to an omitted element forming the ṣila of the relative noun; and فرحون is the predicate of كل. The sentence is explicative, confirming what precedes.

dervis-irab:33-37.t:
* Vocabulary:
(سُلْطاناً): al-sulṭān is proof (ḥujja); you say "he has a clear sulṭān", i.e. clear proof; it also means kingship. The wording of al-Qāmūs is: "al-sulṭān is proof and the power of kingship, and its lām takes ḍamma; and the ruler. It is feminine because it is the plural of salīṭ, for the oil, as if it illuminated; or kingship, or because it means proof; and it may be treated as masculine, going by the sense of 'man'." And in al-Asās: "He has authority over them", "and I had no authority over you" ... "he has a clear sulṭān": a proof. "Sanābik sulṭāt" means long hooves. Al-Jaʿdī said, describing a horse:
مدلّا على سلطات النسو ... رشمّ السنابك لم تقلب
(Roughly: "Confident upon long-hoofed legs, with hooves marked, never turned back.") And he anointed its lamp-wick with salīṭ, which is good oil." Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "al-sulṭān is treated as masculine because it means evidence (dalīl), and as feminine because it means proof (ḥujja); it was also said that it is the plural of salīṭ, like raghīf, pl. rughfān." (يَقْنَطُونَ): they despair of mercy. In al-Miṣbāḥ: it is with fatḥa or kasra on the nūn, both being among the seven readings, and its pattern is ḍaraba and taʿiba. In al-Qāmūs: "qaniṭa like naṣara, ḍaraba, ḥasiba and karuma, verbal noun qunūṭ, and like fariḥa, verbal noun qanaṭ and qanāṭa, and like manaʿa and ḥasiba (these two combine the two dialects): he despaired, so he is qaniṭ like fariḥ; and qannaṭahu taqnīṭan: he made him despair. Al-qanṭ is also withholding, and the raisins of a child." [Translator's note: the source text of this lexical quotation is slightly garbled and its wording is rendered as written.]

* I'rab:
(وَإِذا مَسَّ النَّاسَ ضُرٌّ دَعَوْا رَبَّهُمْ مُنِيبِينَ إِلَيْهِ) A resumptive sentence, introduced to depict the fickle nature of people and their wavering between hope and despair. إذا is an adverb of future time containing the sense of a condition, and the clause مس is in the position of the genitive by the adverb's annexation to it. الناس is a fronted direct object, and ضر a postponed agent. The clause دعوا ربهم has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition. ربهم is a direct object, منيبين is a ḥāl from the agent of دعوا, and إليه is attached to منيبين. (ثُمَّ إِذا أَذاقَهُمْ مِنْهُ رَحْمَةً إِذا فَرِيقٌ مِنْهُمْ بِرَبِّهِمْ يُشْرِكُونَ) ثم is a conjunction of order and delay. إذا is conditional, and the clause أذاقهم is in the position of the genitive by the annexation of the adverb to it. منه is a ḥāl, because it was originally an adjective of رحمة; رحمة is the second direct object. إذا is the sudden إذا (al-fujāʾiyya), which links the apodosis of the first إذا to its condition, so it takes the place of the fāʾ in linking. فريق is the subject, منهم an adjective, بربهم is attached to يشركون, and the clause يشركون is the predicate.
(لِيَكْفُرُوا بِما آتَيْناهُمْ فَتَمَتَّعُوا فَسَوْفَ تَعْلَمُونَ) The lām denotes reason, or consequence and outcome; it was also said that it is the lām of command, the intended sense of the command being threat and warning. يكفروا is an imperfect verb in the subjunctive by an implied أن after the lām. بما is attached to يكفروا, and the clause آتيناهم is the ṣila. فتمتعوا: the fāʾ is a conjunction, and تمتعوا is an imperative verb in which there is a shift from the third person to the second person (iltifāt), to be emphatic in rebuking them; and the fāʾ occurs in the response to the command. سوف is a particle of futurity, and تعلمون is an imperfect verb in the nominative, the wāw its agent. (أَمْ أَنْزَلْنا عَلَيْهِمْ سُلْطاناً فَهُوَ يَتَكَلَّمُ بِما كانُوا بِهِ يُشْرِكُونَ) أم is a disjoined (munqaṭiʿa) conjunction, so it has the sense of "rather" (bal). أنزلنا is a verb and its agent, عليهم is attached to أنزلنا, and سلطانا is a direct object. The fāʾ is a conjunction, هو is the subject, and the clause يتكلم is the predicate. بما is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يتكلم, and the clause كانوا is the ṣila. It is also permissible that ما be a maṣdar, with kāna and its noun, and به attached to يشركون, and the clause يشركون the predicate of كانوا.
(وَإِذا أَذَقْنَا النَّاسَ رَحْمَةً فَرِحُوا بِها) Conjoined to what precedes. The clause فرحوا بها has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition, and the clause أذقنا is in the position of the genitive by the annexation of the adverb to it. (وَإِنْ تُصِبْهُمْ سَيِّئَةٌ بِما قَدَّمَتْ أَيْدِيهِمْ إِذا هُمْ يَقْنَطُونَ) Also conjoined. تصبهم is the protasis, سيئة is the agent, the bāʾ is causal, and ما is a relative noun in the position of the genitive by the bāʾ; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to تصبهم, and the clause قدمت has no position. إذا is the sudden إذا, which has taken the place of the fāʾ in linking the apodosis to the condition; هم is the subject, and the clause يقنطون is the predicate; and the clause إذا هم يقنطون is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis. (أَوَلَمْ يَرَوْا أَنَّ اللَّهَ يَبْسُطُ الرِّزْقَ لِمَنْ يَشاءُ وَيَقْدِرُ) The hamza is for rhetorical interrogation conveying affirmation, and the wāw is conjoined to an omitted element that the context requires. لم is a particle of negation, inversion and jussion, and يروا is an imperfect verb jussive by لم. أن and what falls within its scope stand in place of the two objects of يروا; أن and its noun, and the clause يبسط الرزق is its predicate. لمن is attached to يبسط, the clause يشاء is the ṣila, and يقدر is conjoined to يبسط. (إِنَّ فِي ذلِكَ لَآياتٍ لِقَوْمٍ يُؤْمِنُونَ) The i'rab of its like has been given many times before.

* Rhetoric:
In His words (أَمْ أَنْزَلْنا عَلَيْهِمْ سُلْطاناً فَهُوَ يَتَكَلَّمُ) there is a rational figurative usage (majāz ʿaqlī), as when you say "his book speaks of such-and-such". This is among what the Qur'an has itself expressed with "speaking"; its meaning is indication and testimony, so it testifies to their polytheism, or to that which they associate (with Allah).
